_note: PURGED 2026-08-24 (Sprint 16 closed, v0.1.15 tagged): the ten Sprint 16 items are snapshotted verbatim in archive/backlog-purged-2026-08-24.json and are NOT open work. The hot file now holds only BL-595 (designed, no sprint yet) -- author the next sprint's items fresh against the authority docs when one is picked. File nothing here that the open sprint does not need. Ids never reuse.
Canonical backlog for Project Io — the authoritative METADATA index of every backlog item.
One item = one object in `items`.
STATUS (authoritative; JSON wins over any prose/glyph disagreement):
designed    (glyph ✓) — design settled, promote-ready.
design-owed (glyph ~) — design still owed; must be settled before promotion.
PRIORITY (ascending): F C B A S SSS.
F=deferred/parked, C=low, B=medium, A=important, S=high, SSS=do-immediately.
`parked:true` is the explicit flag for F-priority items.
DIFFICULTY (1-5): 1=~5min, 2=~20min, 3=~1h, 4=~3h, 5=~12h+ (break a 5 down).
SEQUENCING: `requires` lists BL-XXX ids of backlog items that must land first (supercedes the
old `waits_on` short_name list — v2 schema 2026-06-17). `blocked_on` names a truly-external
prerequisite with no backlog item (third-party dep, real-world gate). An item can be `designed`
and still have unmet `requires`. Both fields are nullable; [] means no dependencies.
WORKFLOW: a `designed` item is PROMOTED into REFINED.md and DELIVERED (see DELIVERY.md).
A `design-owed` item is DESIGNED first (prose settled in `design` field, status flipped).
When work lands, the item is RETAINED here under the terminal status `complete` with a
resolution/completion_note, and design propagates into the authority doc. (Convention updated
2026-07-04: terminal items were once removed; the tooling — gyre.py, progress counts — now
depends on them staying. Do not delete landed entries.)
(Terminal status normalised 2026-08-01: `complete` is the only one. `shipped` was a
synonym with no defined difference — written only by tools/session/ship_items.js and
apply_session_close.js, which now write `complete`; the six items carrying it were
converted. Readers still tolerate the old value, so nothing breaks on an old branch.)
DESIGN PROSE — the `design` field (policy updated 2026-06-17):
- ALL items: prose lives in the `design` field here, not in BACKLOG.md.
- NEW items: author prose here directly. No BACKLOG.md body.
- LEGACY items (pre-2026-06-17): `design: "@BACKLOG.md"` means prose is still in markdown.
Migrate to this field on first edit (design settle or promotion) — do not wait for promotion.
On migration: write prose here, replace the BACKLOG.md body with a tombstone line.
- ON PROMOTION into REFINED.md: delete any remaining BACKLOG.md body (if not yet migrated).
- BACKLOG.md therefore only drains, never grows, and is deleted once empty.
- For designs with rich tables use markdown in the `design` string (tables render fine).
- `design: "@<doc>"` is also valid as a pointer to an authority doc when prose lives there.
VERSION GOAL (policy added 2026-07-08): every NEW item names which version it is FOR via the
`version_goal` field — the minor it targets ("v0.0.9"), the next one ("v0.1.0"), or
"post-v0.1.0" for anything beyond the prototype's remaining arc (see ROADMAP.md for the
live version sequence and themes). This is a goal, not a promise — it may slip a version at
re-sequencing, same as priority. Legacy items predating this policy are not backfilled; treat
a missing `version_goal` as "unset (legacy)", not as "post-v0.1.0".
ARCHIVE — the hot/cold split (policy added 2026-08-02):
This file is the METADATA INDEX and is read ACROSS items far more often than INTO one.
So when an item lands, its narrative fields — design, resolution, completion_note,
progress_note — MOVE OUT to docs/development/archive/backlog-design-<quarter>.json.
The item keeps `design: "@<that path>"` (the pointer form blessed above) plus an
`archived` field naming the cold file. This is the authority time-slice made physical:
backlog.json owns the item while it is open; the cold store and the subject authority
doc own it once it has landed.
- Run it: tools/session/archive_designs.js (Delivery close step, after ship_items.js).
- Read it back: tools/session/backlog_query.js --full, or backlog_view.js — both resolve
the pointer transparently, so an archived item reads exactly like a hot one.
- Reverse it: archive_designs.js --restore [BL-XXX ...]. Nothing is ever deleted.
- AMEND A LANDED ITEM'S PROSE IN THE COLD FILE, not here — the hot file has no copy.
- backlog_lint.js FAILS on an `archived` pointer with no record behind it, and WARNS
when frozen history climbs back over 30% of this file.
AUTHOR (policy added 2026-08-22): items may carry an `author` field naming who
proposed the item (e.g. "Joe"). Informational only — no effect on status, priority,
or workflow. Nullable; missing/null means unattributed (legacy items). Design
brainstorms that haven't yet become a backlog item live in docs/development/design/.

items.title: Generation credits every nation's starting treasury before garrison sizing and contract-offer funding read it
items.author: Ben
items.design: Ruled 2026-08-24 (NR-580): a generation-time levy/tariff pass credits every nation's `nation_component::treasury` before `seed_nation_garrisons` (BL-571) and before any contract-offer derivation (BL-572) can run — the same conservation-checked transfer `apply_budget`'s levy already uses, fired once at world creation off whatever each nation's own resource/territory profile earns that first quarter. No new authored number; a rich nation starts richer because its profile already says so. Design settled in `docs/generation/NATION_GENERATION.md` § Pass 7 and `docs/politics/NATIONS.md` § 2 — read those before implementing. Not yet built: every garrison and offer in a freshly generated world still lands on its funding floor today.

items.author: Ben
items.title: Active Logistic Points price the march — the bifold rate lands with its first consumer
items.design: Ruled 2026-08-24 (Sprint 18 design form: shape A, active first): the LP substrate and its FIRST consumer land together, per settled rule 3 — read docs/economy/LOGISTICS.md § Logistic Points whole before implementing; all seven cut constraints bind. Cities generate the bifold per-tick rate (a RATE, not a stock: computed, spent or wasted, never banked, never serialised, no state_hash entry). Active LP prices run_unit_march in credits — march points still spend against traversal cost; active LP is what makes that march cost money (the 2026-08-22 ruling). A refused march is announced, never silently queued. Allocation is a deterministic priority over sorted city ids. First-cut rates authored here, argued against BL-543 (value anchor) and flagged for tuning (NR-600). Fresh authoring: BL-464 and the purged Sprint 32 item prose are reference only. Harness: generation determinism across two runs of one seed, march debit exactness, a refusal mutates nothing. COMPLETE 2026-08-24 (Sprint 18 wave 2, built in place on main): active_lp_anchor_pools (logistics.cpp/hpp), run_unit_march gated on nearest-anchor active LP with credit debit, refused draws mutate nothing (unit_march_tick::refused_no_lp). First-cut rates in scripts/economy.lua (NR-600). Verified independently: logistic_points_harness 27/27 fresh rebuild; unit_march_harness 89/90, the one failure (corp_verb_count staleness) confirmed pre-existing since Sprint 16's BL-573, unrelated; full ProjectIo rebuild clean. NR-619 filed for the nearest-anchor interpretation and refusal-surfacing gap (owed to BL-598). Commit 3cd0204c.

items.author: Ben
items.title: Passive Logistic Points cap convoy admissibility, and war flips the queue
items.design: The second consumer, same sprint (active landed first by ruling). Passive LP caps the automatic trade flow: each dispatch leg draws passive throughput at its route’s city loci; an over-cap leg is REFUSED outright and announced (a refusal nobody sees is silent interdiction again), never queued or clamped. LP is a cap, not a price — credits stay the price (settled rule 1). With both halves live, the built mobilised-first visit order (economy_system.cpp § run order) finally contends for a real pool: goods-vs-force priority becomes an explicit design instead of a tick-phase accident. Harness: admit/refuse boundary exactness, order-independence under contention (two iteration orders, one allocation), the queue flip observable under mobilisation.

items.title: The scorer directs convoys through the shared seam

items.title: The Port building gates the sea leg
items.design: Park lifted 2026-08-24 (design form; the coastal-ports design was parked 2026-08-21). Scope is the GATE: author the Port building (already named in reach’s anchor vocabulary, LOGISTICS.md §3), enforce the two-endpoint check at dispatch, surface the refusal.
